faq.a: The All-India Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers (AICPI-IW) is calculated and released monthly by the Labour Bureau, an attached office of the Ministry of Labour & Employment, Government of India.

Dearness Allowance (DA) for Central Government employees and Dearness Relief (DR) for pensioners are revised twice a year, effective from January 1st and July 1st. The announcements are typically made a few months later.

faq.q: Does DA count towards HRA or other allowances?
faq.a: No, Dearness Allowance (DA) is a separate component and generally does not directly count towards the calculation of other allowances like House Rent Allowance (HRA) or Transport Allowance (TA). These are usually calculated as a percentage of basic pay.
Yes, Dearness Allowance (DA) is fully taxable as part of your salary income under the Income Tax Act, 1961. It is included in your gross salary for tax calculation purposes.

faq.q: Does AICPI-IW impact private sector salaries?
faq.a: While AICPI-IW directly impacts Central Government employees, some public sector undertakings and a few private sector companies may also use it as a reference for wage revisions or cost-of-living adjustments, though it's not universally applied in the private sector.

Dearness Relief (DR) is the equivalent of Dearness Allowance (DA) but is paid to Central Government pensioners. Its purpose and calculation methodology, based on AICPI-IW, are identical to DA, aiming to offset inflation's impact on their pensions.
